title: Fix raw-string-prefix leak in docstring extraction (api_surface.py:652,657) and regenerate affected reference pages
why_root_cause_not_symptom:
Exact bug isolated to two identical lines in _extract_doc_comment() (api_surface.py:652 and :657): `raw = node_text(s).strip("\"' 
")` strips quote/space/newline characters from the tree-sitter-captured docstring text, but does not account for Python's raw-string prefix (r/R, optionally combined with b/B) preceding the quotes. For a docstring literally written as r"""Configuration...""", the leading r blocks .strip() from ever reaching the quote characters, so both the r prefix and the quote marks survive into the extracted 'doc' field verbatim, then flow unmodified into every downstream consumer (batch_reference.py explicitly documents using 'the entry's own scout-extracted doc field' as-is, 'always correct for its own class' -- an assumption this specific case violates).

title: Add a module-compilability evaluator check (no existing evaluator verifies documented public API modules actually import from the pinned clone)
why_root_cause_not_symptom: RC-W1-004 (MT026) added a code-reachability check verifying a cited class/function is exported (__all__, exported_via_package_init) -- but that check assumes the module containing it can be imported at all. It does not, and no other evaluator does either, attempt to actually compile/import the documented public API module against the pinned clone. tex/python's presentation/__init__.py (the module defining TeXJob, TeXOptions, and all 3 output devices) fails py_compile with IndentationError -- 35/45 files in the whole package fail identically -- yet every evaluator that ran (audit.py, gap-eval) returned clean/near-clean results for pages built entirely around this non-importable module, because none of them try to import it. NOTE: the underlying source defect is upstream (confirmed via git show HEAD: -- the pinned commit itself, not a clone-cache artifact) and is not something this pipeline can or should fix (clone cache is read-only per AGENTS.md 2a) -- this taskcard's scope is limited to adding the missing evaluator check itself, not to fixing tex/python's upstream source.

title: FND-tex-python-007 (load_format inconsistency): root cause not isolated after real investigation -- deferred, not dropped
pause_reason: products.aspose.org/en/tex/python/_index.md's 3 code examples correctly use TeXOptions(load_format=False), matching the source docstring's documented current limitation; every other page (docs/kb/blog, ~25 pages) uses bare TeXOptions() defaults instead. Checked whether new-products-page.md's skill instructions explicitly require load_format=False (they do not -- 0 matches) and whether this is a generation-skill difference; found no single skill instruction or extraction field that would explain why one generation path got this right and the others did not. Given FND-tex-python-008 (the pinned source doesn't compile at all), this cannot currently be resolved empirically either. Deferred pending either a dedicated deeper investigation pass or resolution of FND-008 first (once/if the compile-check-gap taskcard's evaluator work reveals more about how these examples were validated, if at all, at generation time).

title: Fix false PyPI-publication claims and unverifiable format-support table on the tex/python introducing blog post (superseding TC-tex-python-original-item-2's evaluator-extension scope, now known unnecessary)
why_root_cause_not_symptom: CORRECTION to the original diagnosis: install_recipe.py already has _verify_publish_channel_claims (the real RC-W1-003 fix, complete with a PyPI mention_re that matches plain prose, not just install commands) -- confirmed by running `python -m scripts.pipeline.content_eval evaluate` directly, which caught BOTH FND-tex-python-005 instances exactly, plus a finding this batch's unaided pass missed entirely: FND-tex-python-009 (format_truth evaluator) -- the blog post's 'Supported Formats' table shows Write:check for PDF/DVI/SVG, but knowledge/tex/python/merged/formats.json marks all 3 as functional:false (enum_only -- the scout could only confirm they exist as OutputFormat enum members, consistent with FND-008's finding that the source doesn't compile, so nothing about real I/O behavior could be verified). REAL root cause: `audit.py` (scripts/pipeline/commands/content/audit.py, via audit.runner) is a DIFFERENT, narrower tool than `content_eval` (scripts/pipeline/content_eval, which owns install_recipe.py and format_truth) -- confirmed by grep, audit.py never imports content_eval at all. This entire batch's system-review phase used audit.py exclusively, silently under-representing what system tooling actually catches. Compounded by RC-tex-python-04 (missing gap-eval profile for tex/python) -- gap-eval's own multi-tier design is presumably what should dispatch to the full content_eval suite in normal operation, and its degraded 'minimal defaults' fallback means this page was very likely never run through content_eval at all after generation, which is how a live FAIL on a false publication claim survived undetected.
